audits.title: The use of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) principles in Scottish orthopaedic units--an implementation and follow-up at 1 year, 2010-2011: a report from the Musculoskeletal Audit, Scotland.
audits.standard: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) principles for hip and knee arthroplasty
audits.setting: All 22 Scottish orthopaedic units (Musculoskeletal Audit, Scotland)

cycle1.result: 8 (36%) units had an ERAS programme; urinary catheterisation 468/1,345 (35%).

audits.intervention: Input and support from a national steering group (nationally guided ERAS programme).

cycle2.result: 15 (68%) units had an ERAS programme; urinary catheterisation 337/1,278 (26%) (p = 0.03).

audits.other_findings: ERAS patients mobilised same day more often (36% vs 4%), had shorter stay (median 4 vs 5 days) and ERAS knee patients had fewer transfusions (2% vs 13%).
audits.citation: Scott NB, McDonald D, Campbell J, Smith RD, Carey AK, Johnston IG, et al.. The use of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) principles in Scottish orthopaedic units--an implementation and follow-up at 1 year, 2010-2011: a report from the Musculoskeletal Audit, Scotland. Arch Orthop Trauma Surg. 2013;133(1):117-124. doi:10.1007/s00402-012-1619-z. PMID: 23070220.

audits.title: Enhanced recovery from surgery in the UK: an audit of the enhanced recovery partnership programme 2009-2012.
audits.standard: Enhanced Recovery protocol elements; good compliance defined as 80% or more
audits.setting: 61 NHS hospital trusts; colorectal, orthopaedic, urological and gynaecological surgery

cycle1.result: Compliance weakly associated with shorter stay (r -0.18 colorectal, -0.14 orthopaedics, -0.25 gynaecology); 80% compliance linked to 2, 1 and 3 day shorter median stay in colorectal, orthopaedic and urological surgery

audits.other_findings: No length of stay saving in gynaecology.
audits.citation: Simpson JC, Moonesinghe SR, Grocott MP, Kuper M, McMeeking A, Oliver CM, et al.. Enhanced recovery from surgery in the UK: an audit of the enhanced recovery partnership programme 2009-2012. Br J Anaesth. 2015;115(4):560-568. doi:10.1093/bja/aev105. PMID: 25926312.

audits.title: Revolutionising rapid recovery: a quality improvement project in hip and knee replacement.
audits.standard: Local SMART aim: 90% of cases mobilising on day 0 and length of stay reduced by 1 day within 1 year, with increased throughput
audits.setting: North Devon District Hospital, elective hip and knee replacement pathway

cycle1.result: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.

cycle2.result: Mean length of stay fell to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 days for knees (p<0.0001); all patients mobilised on day 0 in the most recent 3 months; predicted yearly throughput 560 vs 480.

audits.other_findings: Trust moved from 41st to 8th (hips) and 34th to 4th (knees) nationally for length of stay; opioid use per patient fell from about 400 mg to under 300 mg morphine equivalent. Only 3.5% of first mobilisations were by a physiotherapist in the latest 3 months.
audits.citation: Parkes RJ, Ayeko O, Brunton L, Griffiths-Jones W, Ungvari Z, Goss H. Revolutionising rapid recovery: a quality improvement project in hip and knee replacement. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(2):e001249. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001249. PMID: 33879494.

audits.title: Mobilisation After Total Knee Replacement Within an Enhanced Recovery Pathway: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Mobilisation within 24 hours after surgery, in keeping with ERAS principles and local pathway expectations
audits.setting: Orthopaedic Department, James Paget University Hospital, Gorleston; enhanced recovery pathway for primary TKR

cycle1.result: 35/53 (66.0%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

audits.intervention: MAKE1 findings presented to the multidisciplinary team; reinforcement of enhanced recovery practices, better documentation of reasons for delayed mobilisation and prompt management/escalation of pain, nausea and hypotension.

cycle2.result: 57/63 (90.5%) mobilised within 24 hours; median length of stay 2 days.

audits.other_findings: Pain remained the commonest barrier and was linked to longer stay (mean 5.2 days in MAKE2). No POD 0 physiotherapy assessments were documented, and no clear difference was seen between spinal and general anaesthesia.
audits.citation: Pantelidou M, Adeyeye A, Khurana D, Pantelidis E. Mobilisation After Total Knee Replacement Within an Enhanced Recovery Pathway: A Two-Cycle Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2026;18(1):e101133. doi:10.7759/cureus.101133. PMID: 41664711.

audits.title: Achieving effective and timely quality of care in same-day discharge total hip arthroplasty without compromising patient safety.
audits.standard: Aim of >80% successful same-day discharge among eligible primary THA patients without compromising safety (unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters)
audits.setting: Vancouver General Hospital arthroplasty service ('Short Term Accelerated Recovery' STAR programme)

cycle1.result: Standard cohort: 57/105 (54.3%) discharged same day; complications preventing same-day discharge 48 (45.7%); unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters 11 (10.5%).

audits.intervention: Enhanced Recovery Canada recommendations: pre-emptive nausea prophylaxis (aprepitant, scopolamine patch), pre-emptive multimodal oral analgesia, and lidocaine epidural anaesthesia via a 'STAR Module' in the electronic order set, supported by STAR rounds, website posts and a video; then a switch to spinal lidocaine.

cycle2.result: Spinal lidocaine cohort: 80.6% discharged same day vs 54.3% (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.34 to 8.66, p=0.0102).

audits.other_findings: Combined ERC cohort (February 2021–August 2024, n=129): 96 (74.4%) same-day discharge (OR 2.51, p=0.0015), complications preventing discharge 33 (25.6%), 30-day encounters 12 (9.3%), not significantly different. Transient neurological symptoms in 3/33 (9%) spinal lidocaine patients; lack of evening physiotherapy limited reassessment.
audits.citation: Young DJ, Hsieh M, Sadiq I, Askari A, Greidanus N. Achieving effective and timely quality of care in same-day discharge total hip arthroplasty without compromising patient safety. BMJ Open Qual. 2026;15(1):e003494. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003494. PMID: 41781148.
